analysis.title: Global Fixed Income Team Outlook & Strategy, Market Recap & Outlook (November 2026)
key_insights: The US 10-year Treasury yield is just under 4.9%, down from 5.3% in early October. Almost half of the summer sell-off has reversed. The team attributes the decline to lower oil and to equity sellers buying Treasuries.

The team calls current yield levels fair. They balance 50bp of expected Fed rate hikes and elevated headline and core PCE inflation against forecasters' growing expectation of falling inflation in 2027.
With headline GDP growth expected to stay firm, the team expects Treasuries, credit spreads and the dollar to be range-bound in the near term.

Brent nearby futures fell $20 to $93 per barrel since Halloween. The team says sentiment has shifted toward an earlier end to the Iran conflict, and rumors of new deals have re-emerged after the failed Memorandum of Understanding.

The team argues high oil prices have driven substitution through electrification, more non-Gulf supply and a revival of Mideast output. OPEC reports October production at 88%-90% of prewar output, led by Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. Brent is only 3% above last May's level, so the oil impulse to inflation is fading.
The US midterms were driven by inflation and affordability, with $4 gasoline and $6 diesel prominent. The team links this to the war with Iran.

After a post-election relief rally, equities sold off semiconductor names on incoming Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, where nearly 50% of data centers sit. A datacenter slowdown would ease hyperscaler cash flow worries but directly slow chip demand.
The Anthropic IPO is flagged as the next event that may influence sentiment on frontier AI revenues and profitability.

The team does not expect a quiet market. They expect the Trump presidency to keep generating volatility, with an opposition Congress an obvious target. Bond supply from unresolved deficits and the AI investment boom could push yields slowly higher and credit spreads slowly wider.
Whether the dollar weakens will depend on equity sentiment and the unknown future profitability of the AI investment boom.

Rising Gulf output, led by Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, adds supply and helps oil prices fall.

risk_factors: Volatility from the Trump presidency, with an opposition Congress an obvious target.
Bond supply from unresolved government deficits and the AI investment boom could push yields slowly higher and credit spreads slowly wider.
Unknown future profitability of the AI investment boom, which the team calls the greatest investment gamble in the history of capitalism, may affect equity sentiment and the dollar.
A datacenter slowdown tied to Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Ohio could directly slow chip demand.
The Iran standoff and the failed Memorandum of Understanding leave the oil path uncertain.
geopolitical: War with Iran: the team says sentiment has shifted toward an earlier end to the conflict, and rumors of new deals have re-emerged after the stillborn Memorandum of Understanding.
Eurasia Group base case had been an upsurge in violence once the US midterms were over.
US midterm elections produced a Blue Wave. Exit polls named inflation and affordability, ICE conduct, Trump family enrichment and data centers as issues.
The team lists tariffs, Greenland, Venezuela and Iran as examples of Trump-era volatility and expects an opposition Congress to be a target.
